q: Name the two Pauillac second growths of the Pichon family split.
accept: pichon-longueville baron and comtesse de lalande
ans: Pichon-Longueville Baron and Pichon-Longueville Comtesse de Lalande
exp: They face each other across the D2 at Latour's shoulder.

q: Cos d'Estournel and Montrose lead which commune's classified growths?
exp: Saint-Estèphe: clay-cooled Cabernet, the sturdiest Médoc wines; no first growths.

q: How many estates were classified Premier Grand Cru Classé 'A' in the 2022 Saint-Émilion revision, and name one of them.
ans: Two: Pavie and Figeac (Ausone, Cheval Blanc and Angélus had withdrawn)
exp: The classification revises ~every decade; the withdrawals headline its politics.

q: Which Pomerol estate, long run by the Moueix family, commands the appellation's highest prices from ~11.5 ha of blue clay?
exp: Near-pure Merlot on the boutonnière of smectite clay; no classification exists in Pomerol.

q: Le Pin, Pomerol's garage-wine pioneer, was founded by which Belgian family in 1979?
exp: ~2.7 ha; with Vieux Château Certan in the same family.

q: Which estate stands alone atop the 1855 Sauternes classification as Premier Cru Supérieur, and in which commune does it lie?
exp: Premier Cru Supérieur — a tier of one.

q: Barsac producers may label under which two AOPs?
exp: The privilege runs one way; Climens and Coutet lead Barsac.

q: What is a 'palus' in Bordeaux vineyard vocabulary?
opts: Drainage channel dug by the Dutch
exp: Rich riverside soils give big yields of light wine; the croupes de graves carry the great estates. Palus land is fertile and damp, and no classified growth sits on it.

q: The Dutch engineering that made the Médoc plantable in the 1600s primarily involved:
ans: Draining the marshes with canal systems
exp: Before drainage the Médoc was salt-marsh; the gravel croupes emerged as vineyard land.

q: Which fifth growth of Pauillac did the Cazes family drive to super-second status?
Match each right-bank name to the appellation family it belongs to.
ans: Lussac–St-Émilion · Néac–Lalande-de-Pomerol · Fronsac–Libournais · Castillon–Côtes de Bordeaux
exp: Lussac, Montagne, Puisseguin and Saint-Georges hyphenate Saint-Émilion; Néac's wines have been sold as Lalande-de-Pomerol since 1954; Fronsac is an independent Libournais appellation, not a satellite; Castillon joined the Côtes de Bordeaux umbrella in 2009.

q: Which grape's Bordeaux plantings collapsed after the 1956 frost, exiling it to Cahors and Argentina?
exp: The frost killed a third of Bordeaux's vines; replanting favored Merlot.

q: Select every legal red-wine grape of AOP Bordeaux from this list.
exp: Touriga Nacional joined 2021's climate-adaptation varieties (with Marselan, Castets, Arinarnoa); Syrah and Tannat remain outside.

q: What does 'en primeur' commit a buyer to?
accept: paying now for wine delivered later
buying futures two years before delivery
ans: Paying for barrel-stage wine delivered ~two years later
exp: The spring tastings after harvest set the campaign; risk trades for allocation and (sometimes) price.

q: Which Margaux third growth, restored by the Le Lous family since 2019, shares its name with a Scottish clan?
exp: Cantenac Brown — John Lewis Brown's legacy; Kirwan is Irish, for the record.

q: Haut-Brion Blanc's neighbor and rival on the Pessac plateau — the classified white of the pair — is:
ans: La Mission Haut-Brion Blanc (formerly Laville Haut-Brion)
exp: Sémillon-led, among the world's priciest dry whites; note Haut-Brion Blanc itself is unclassified — only Laville/La Mission Blanc appears among the nine crus classés de Graves for white.
